stories.headline: India rejects US 'excess capacity' charge; US offers 17% tariff with deal, 25% without
stories.summary: The Commerce Department said India has no structural excess capacity in any sector and that the US notice is under examination. It wants trade concerns settled inside the bilateral trade deal talks. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said India's rate would be capped at 17% if a deal is reached and rise to 25% without one. Change since last edition: India's response and its proposed tariff rates.
stories.why_it_matters: A deal at 17% would leave Indian goods slightly cheaper than rivals such as Vietnam, Thailand and Bangladesh in the US market.
stories.note: The trade research group GTRI says the 17% deal rate gives India a 1-3 point edge over Asian rivals.

impact.why: Exporters face up to 25% US duty, but a trade deal would cap it at 17%.
Tariff risk weighs on the rupee; hopes of a deal soften it.

stories.headline: Net FDI turns negative: $4.9 billion flowed out in September, a 5.5-year low
stories.summary: RBI data show gross FDI inflows of $5.9 billion in September were beaten by $6.5 billion of repatriation, and Indian firms invested another $4.4 billion abroad. That left a net outflow of about $4.95 billion, the weakest month since at least March 2021. For April to September, net FDI was still higher at $8.8 billion, against $7.4 billion a year earlier.
stories.why_it_matters: Weaker long-term foreign investment leaves the rupee more dependent on volatile share-market flows.

impact.why: Net FDI outflows reduce steady dollar supply for the rupee.

stories.headline: MEA says Indian and Chinese armies held high-level border talks in Arunachal
stories.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs said senior commanders met this month in the Arunachal Pradesh sector to discuss border management and open issues on the Line of Actual Control. The talks came amid reports of aggressive Chinese troop moves near Upper Subansiri.

stories.headline: Duty-free raw sugar imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes extended to March 2027
stories.summary: The DGFT extended the window for duty-free raw sugar imports under the tariff-rate quota from December 31 to the end of March 2027. Mills have until September 30, 2027 to refine and sell the imported sugar.

impact.why: More cheap raw sugar can help refiners but cap local sugar prices.

stories.headline: Saudi-led coalition says Houthis hit Jizan port and fired missiles at Riyadh
stories.summary: The coalition says a Houthi projectile hit Jizan port on the Red Sea, causing minor damage, and that it shot down a drone over Jeddah port and ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh. An explosion was then heard in Sanaa. The Houthis had threatened Saudi ports after new strikes on Yemen's Hodeidah port. Change since last edition: attacks spread from Ras Tanura to Red Sea ports and the capital.
stories.why_it_matters: Attacks on Saudi ports and cities add risk to Gulf oil and Red Sea shipping that India relies on.
stories.note: Claims by the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis; damage not independently confirmed.

image.alt: A man searches the rubble of a destroyed telecom building in Hodeidah, Yemen

impact.why: Strikes near Saudi ports and Riyadh raise supply risk.

stories.headline: Israeli judges urge prosecutors to drop Netanyahu bribery charge
stories.summary: Judges told the attorney general there was little chance of conviction in Case 4000, where Benjamin Netanyahu is accused of trading favours for good media coverage. They also doubted a second case and suggested a plea deal in the third. The caretaker prime minister called for the trial to end at once.

stories.headline: Ukraine says it hit five Russian jets at Savasleyka airbase east of Moscow
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff says three MiG-31s, which carry Kinzhal hypersonic missiles, and two Su-34 bombers were damaged at the airbase in the Nizhny Novgorod region. Kyiv also says it struck two oil refineries in Russia's Samara region. Russia did not comment at once.
stories.note: Claim by Ukraine's General Staff; not independently confirmed.

stories.headline: Fuel tanker fire on Cairo ring road kills about 30 people
stories.summary: A truck carrying fuel overturned and caught fire on a busy ring road in Cairo, killing at least 30 people and injuring more. It is the latest in a series of deadly transport disasters in Egypt.
stories.note: BBC reports 31 dead and 21 injured; Al Jazeera at least 30 dead and 15 injured.

stories.headline: RBI bought a net $6.94 billion in September; forward dollar book hits record
stories.summary: RBI Bulletin data show the central bank bought $82.18 billion and sold $75.25 billion in September, its fourth straight month of net buying after a record $43.26 billion in August. Its net short dollar position in forwards rose about $39 billion to a record $239.18 billion. Net buying so far this financial year is $54.37 billion.
stories.why_it_matters: Heavy RBI dollar buying shows it is capping rupee gains and rebuilding reserves while inflows are strong.
stories.note: Single source: Business Standard, citing RBI Bulletin data.

impact.why: RBI buying dollars limits how far the rupee can rise.

stories.headline: RBI moves 60 tonnes of gold home; 84% of its gold now kept in India
stories.summary: The RBI's half-yearly reserves report shows 740.13 tonnes of its 880.52 tonnes of gold held in India at end-September, up from 680.05 tonnes in March. Gold kept with the Bank of England and BIS fell to 140.39 tonnes. Total forex reserves stood at $737.78 billion at end-September, up from $691.11 billion.
stories.note: The value of the gold fell to $106.08 billion from $115.40 billion as prices dropped, per Business Standard.

stories.headline: Dollar slips as stocks recover; yen and Swiss franc gain
stories.summary: The dollar index fell about 0.2% to near 103.6 late on Wednesday after first rising as AI stocks tumbled. The dollar lost 0.6% against the Swiss franc to 0.83, and the yen edged up to 159.13 per dollar. Traders are weighing how many more Fed rate hikes are coming after hot inflation data.

impact.why: A late stock rebound cut safe-haven demand for the dollar.

stories.headline: Update: Wall Street claws back from 4% Nasdaq plunge; Dow ends higher
stories.summary: Bargain hunters cut most of Wednesday's losses. The S&P 500 closed 0.25% lower at 7,182.78 and the Nasdaq 0.6% lower at 23,585.80, after the Nasdaq had been down more than 4% and the Nasdaq 100 briefly 20% below its record. The Dow rose 0.3% to 50,182.95. Nvidia fell about 4-5%. US markets are shut on Thursday for Thanksgiving.
stories.why_it_matters: The late US recovery takes some pressure off Indian IT and tech shares at today's open.
stories.note: Closing levels from Yahoo Finance; an early Reuters tally (Dow 50,365.85, Nasdaq 23,611.61) differs slightly.

image.alt: Traders gesture on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange

impact.why: Steep intraday swings show AI stocks remain fragile.
A late Wall Street rebound eases pressure on Indian IT.

stories.headline: Asian stocks rebound over 1%; Bank of Korea raises rate to 3.25%
stories.summary: Japan's Nikkei rose about 1.4% to near 57,790 and Korea's Kospi about 1.3% in early Thursday trade, following Wall Street's comeback. The Bank of Korea raised its key rate by 0.25 point to 3.25%, a two-year high, as inflation and Seoul house prices stay high. Kospi had fallen 6.2% on Wednesday.
stories.note: Single source for the Bank of Korea decision: Mint. Index levels from Yahoo Finance.

impact.why: Firmer Asian markets support a steady start in India.

stories.headline: Gold steadies near $3,590 after MCX futures hit a one-year low
stories.summary: MCX gold futures fell as much as 3.6% to ₹1,17,906 per 10 grams on Wednesday, their lowest in over a year, and silver dropped to ₹1,36,712 per kg as hot US inflation lifted Fed hike bets. Overseas, gold futures recovered to about $3,588 an ounce in early Asian trade on Thursday, up about 0.6%.
stories.note: MCX levels are intraday lows from Mint; global price from Yahoo Finance.

impact.why: Fed hike bets weigh on gold, but bargain buying lifted it overnight.

stories.headline: FCC clears SpaceX to launch up to 1 million 'Starmind' data-centre satellites
stories.summary: US regulators approved SpaceX's plan for solar-powered satellites that process AI computing in orbit, the first approval of its kind. The first satellites must fly by 2033 and the full network by 2040. Amazon, Viasat and astronomers had opposed it.
stories.why_it_matters: It opens a new race to move AI computing off the ground, away from power-hungry land data centres.

image.alt: A SpaceX Starship rocket lifts off beside its launch tower

impact.why: Approval backs SpaceX's plan for orbital AI data centres.

stories.headline: Roche wins FDA nod for first new early breast cancer hormone pill in 20 years
stories.summary: The FDA approved Roche's Wilserdly (giredestrant), a once-daily pill, for stage I to III ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer at higher risk of return. In the lidERA trial it cut the risk of cancer coming back or death by 30% versus standard hormone therapy.
stories.note: Approved on November 23; overall survival benefit not yet shown.

impact.why: A new approved use widens the drug's market.

forex_results.title: Core PCE Price Index m/m
forex_results.why: Core prices rose 0.3% as expected, but the yearly rate climbed to 3.3%, keeping a December Fed hike near-certain.

forex_results.title: Prelim GDP q/q
forex_results.why: Growth was revised up to 4.3% from 3.4%, above the 3.5% forecast, which supports the dollar and Fed hike bets.

forex_results.title: Monetary Policy Report Hearings
forex_results.why: Bailey said further hikes are more likely than not if energy prices stay high, which supports the pound.
